unpleasant.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with itch, which is an unpleasant feeling on your skin.
unpleasant.zh: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with itch, which is an unpleasant feeling on your skin.

unpleasant.en: We're talking about itching. Now an itch is that unpleasant feeling you get on your skin that you have to scratch with your fingers.
unpleasant.zh: We're talking about itching. Now an itch is that unpleasant feeling you get on your skin that you have to scratch with your fingers.

unexpected.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the unexpected return of nuclear power.
unexpected.zh: 好的，关于核电出人意料强势回归的这期节目就到这里。

unexpected.en: So the world's biggest technology companies did something unexpected, or I guess rather obvious when you understand that electricity is their biggest constraint .
unexpected.zh: 于是，全球最大的科技公司做了一件出人意料的事，或者说，当你明白电力是他们最大的瓶颈时，这其实是顺理成章的。

uncomfortable.en: It's uncomfortable. Sometimes, though, it happens.
uncomfortable.zh: 这让人感到尴尬。不过有时，这种情况确实会发生。

uncertain.en: In January of this year, January of 2026, the German Chancellor, Friedrich Merz, stood in front of the Chamber of Industry and Commerce in Dessau and admitted, in no uncertain terms , that his country, Germany, had made a mistake.
uncertain.zh: 今年1月，也就是2026年1月，德国总理 Friedrich Merz 站在德绍工商会面前，毫不含糊地承认他的国家——德国，犯了一个错误。

unite.en: Data centres in the United States now use more than 4% of the country's entire electricity supply.
unite.zh: 美国的数据中心目前消耗了该国全社会用电量的4%以上。

unite.en: Take the United States. Pizza is very strongly associated with New York food culture, even though pizza is an Italian food, originated in Italy.
unite.zh: 以美国为例。披萨与纽约饮食文化紧密相连，尽管披萨是意大利食物，起源于意大利。

unite.en: Add it all together, and the nuclear capacity now committed to data centres by these companies is up to 13 gigawatts , and that is just in the United States.
unite.zh: 总而言之，这些公司目前承诺为数据中心提供的核电容量已高达13吉瓦，而这仅仅是在美国。

unusual.en: This isn’t unusual. Most countries around the world have incorporated foods introduced by immigrants.
unusual.zh: 这并不罕见。世界上大多数国家都融入了移民引入的食物。

unusual.en: Some foods were completely unavailable. This produced a very unusual food culture.
unusual.zh: 有些食物完全买不到。这产生了一种非常不寻常的饮食文化。

universally.en: Rationing, though, did not mean that British food became universally terrible.
universally.zh: 然而，配给并不意味着英国食物变得一无是处。

university.en: They just complained about it. I took them to a farmers market that popped up near the university every Wednesday, and I bought them some pies.
university.zh: 他们只是盲目抱怨。于是我带他们去了每周三在大学附近摆摊的农贸市场，给他们买了几只派。
